name: Phyllodes Tumor of the Breast

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Phyllodes Tumor

criteria.description: Presence of stromal hypercellularity with leaf-like architecture
Increased mitotic activity in stromal cells (>5 mitoses per 10 high power fields)
Stromal overgrowth defined as absence of epithelial elements in at least one low power field

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of stromal hypercellularity with leaf-like architecture and increased mitotic activity
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires tissue biopsy and histological examination; imaging alone is insufficient.

searchTerms: smooth breast mass with clear edges

common.symptomName: Breast skin stretching or thinning over tumor
searchTerms: skin thinning or stretching over breast tumor
breast skin changes due to underlying lump
skin dimpling or thinning on breast

common.symptomName: Breast asymmetry due to mass effect

occasional.symptomName: Breast pain unrelated to menstrual cycle
searchTerms: breast pain not linked to period

laboratory: Histopathological examination showing biphasic tumor with epithelial and stromal components
Increased mitotic figures in stromal cells
imaging: Ultrasound showing well-circumscribed, hypoechoic mass with cystic spaces
Mammography revealing large, round or oval mass with smooth or lobulated margins
MRI demonstrating heterogeneous enhancement with internal septations
genetic: MED12 gene mutations frequently observed in stromal component
Chromosomal abnormalities including gains in 1q and 5p
other: Gross pathology shows leaf-like projections on cut section
Tumor size often >3 cm at diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Slower growth rate compared to phyllodes tumor
Lack of stromal overgrowth and mitotic activity
Smaller size and more common in younger women
Malignant epithelial cells with invasive features
Often associated with nipple retraction and skin changes
Signs of infection such as erythema, warmth, and systemic symptoms
Rapid onset and response to antibiotics

redFlags: Rapid increase in breast mass size over weeks
Skin ulceration or necrosis over tumor
Fixation of mass to underlying chest wall or skin
references: Tan PH, et al. Phyllodes Tumors of the Breast: Pathology, Diagnosis, and Management. Surg Pathol Clin. 2019.
